newsitem.title: MEXICO: FOCUS - Televisa unveils cost-cutting plan.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Televisa unveils cost-cutting plan.

text.p: Mexico's Grupo Televisa SA on Wednesday unveiled a massive restructuring plan to cut costs, spruce up its television programming and convince skeptics it will remain the Spanish-speaking world's leading media company.
The Televisa 2000 plan calls for $270 million in cuts over the next three years through a combination of layoffs and belt-tightening moves at each of its units, the company said in a statement.

It also pledged to shareholders and analysts in a New York meeting on Wednesday to polish its television programming and modernize its news division to fend off upstart rival TV Azteca, which has steadily stolen market share from Televisa.

The moves were aimed at shoring up confidence in the company that was hit by the death in April of its patriarch Emilio Azcarraga Milmo and the rise to power of his relatively inexperienced 29-year-old son Emilio Azcarraga Jean.

"Televisa has three specific goals: improve its television ratings, build out its direct to home satellite television business and significantly improve its financial performance," Chairman Emilio Azcarraga Jean said.
Investors welcomed the news. Televisa's American Depositary Receipts rose 9.3 percent to $27.875 on the New York Stock Exchange on Wednesday.

"People feel a bit more positive (about the company). If (Televisa) can stick to these initiatives, they are clearly on the right track," said Marla Marron, an analyst at ING Barings in New York who attended a meeting there on Wednesday between Televisa and shareholders and analysts.
Televisa did not say how many jobs would be lost, but said it would take a one-time $80 million charge mostly due to severance and termination costs of senior executives and their staff.

It also said it would freeze executive salaries and introduce a new compensation policy for executives that replaces salary increases with stock options, tying the company's performance to wage gains.

"They are now cutting fat from the higher levels of the company that were left largely untouched by the previous cost-cutting plan (implemented in 1994)," Francisco Rivero, an analyst at Valores Finamex in New York, told Reuters.

Televisa will also trim its $988 million in total debt by $100 million using part of the $650 million it recently received for selling its stake in PanAmSat Corp SPOT.O. The move will lower its interest expense for 1997 to between $135-$145 million compared to about $245 million in 1996.

"Through a combination of the strengthening Mexican economy, cost-cutting measures and efforts to increase revenues, the company expects its cash flow margins to exceed 25 percent," CEO Guillermo Canedo White said.

Programming head Jaime Davila told investors Televisa will present a slew of innovative programs later this year to halt the slide in market share and cash in on its year-end advertising plan, according to analysts.
Televisa said it had signed up 30,000 subscribers to date for its Sky satellite television project, a joint venture with News Corp, and was gaining 400-500 new subscribers a day, according to Marron.
Although the moves assuaged some worries about the company, analysts said it will still have to prove there is life beyond Azcarraga Milmo and that it can react to Azteca's challenge.
"One presentation will not change the expectations dramatically. Azcarraga Jean has to build up an image and a career and it won't happen from dusk till dawn," Rivero said.
